title: The canvas widgets decide in their rows too: Decide nowhere on the surface
purpose: Tom's reading of 18 October 2026 took the Decide button off the dashboard: a request or a draft is approved or declined in the row it stands in, never on another page. DIRECTORY-104 landed that on the dashboard's own list, and found on its way out that the canvas's widgets, which draw the same requests and drafts in a window a person places, still end every row in a Decide link to another page (Widgets.tsx lines 50 and 65). The same thing on two screens is decided two ways. This brief makes the widgets decide where they stand with the same forms the dashboard uses, so the word Decide is gone from the surface.
task: Give requestsPart and draftsPart the person and a changed callback, draw DecisionForm and DraftDecide in their rows exactly as WaitingOnYou's Row does, move sourceWords to waiting.ts so both import it, pass the canvas's person and re-read through CanvasWidgets.tsx, pin it red first in canvas-parts.test.tsx, and prove the word Decide appears as no label anywhere under surface/identity/src.

requirements.title: The requests and drafts widgets decide in their rows, the way the dashboard's rows do
requirements.spec: Behavioural. In surface/identity/src/features/dashboard/Widgets.tsx, requestsPart takes requests, me and changed and draws each waiting request's row as the dashboard's row draws a request entry (WaitingOnYou.tsx, Row): the asker, what for and why, then, where the person may decide it (can_decide, else the approvers naming them), DecisionForm from features/requests/DecisionForm.tsx built from the request itself (person = me, canIssueRoot = request.can_issue_root === true, changed, describe = sourceWords), so the acts Approve access and Decline request stand in the row; where the person may not decide it, the approvers' names as today. draftsPart takes drafts, me and changed and draws each draft's row with DraftDecide from features/drafts/DraftDecide.tsx (draft, person = me, changed), so Approve and Decline stand in the row. sourceWords moves out of WaitingOnYou.tsx into surface/identity/src/features/dashboard/waiting.ts (exported) and both WaitingOnYou.tsx and Widgets.tsx import it, so the dashboard and the canvas say a source grant the same way. surface/identity/src/features/runtime/CanvasWidgets.tsx passes board.me and a changed that re-reads the board the canvas holds (the read in surface/identity/src/features/dashboard/board.ts), the way the canvas already re-reads it; where the canvas has no such re-read, one re-read of that board on changed is added and the report names it. No link or button on the dashboard or the canvas reads Decide: the dashboard's requests page is still reached from the widget's own heading link (#/requests, #/access/drafts), never from a row.
acceptance: Red first, in surface/identity/src/features/dashboard/canvas-parts.test.tsx: a waiting request the person may decide draws, in its row, the acts by aria-label Approve access and Decline request and no link whose text is Decide; a waiting request the person may not decide draws the approvers' names and no act; a draft's row draws Approve and Decline by aria-label and no link whose text is Decide; the counts in the headings are unchanged
surface/identity/tests/canvas-widgets.test.tsx stays green against the new props, its assertions kept and extended only where a widget's row changed
grep -rn '>Decide<' surface/identity/src answers nothing, and the report says so with the command
gate -stages tsc,vitest -dir surface/identity: tsc 0 findings, every vitest file green, the counts in the report

boundaries: Who may decide a request or a draft is unchanged; the widget draws the form the requests and drafts pages already use, it decides nothing itself
No new read: the canvas reads the board it reads today; changed re-reads it, nothing polls
No timer, no fixed wait, no poll and no deadline anywhere, in code or test
The dashboard's own list (WaitingOnYou.tsx) changes only by importing sourceWords from waiting.ts; its tests are untouched and green
Nothing in lys-pass, nothing installed, the installed Lys untouched
Every file touched stays under 500 code lines (ADR-111, by scripts/file-length.sh)
verification: python3 scripts/design/validate.py docs/design/directory and python3 scripts/design/check-coverage.py docs/design/directory read for FAIL lines
